t: Under Section 2(7)(ii), a person who 'hires or avails of any services' for consideration is a consumer. Which of the following is therefore a consumer vis-à-vis an insurer?
o: A surveyor engaged by the insurer
A TPA under contract with the insurer
A policyholder who has paid premium for a mediclaim policy
e: A policyholder hires the insurer's service for consideration (premium) and is a consumer; reinsurers, surveyors and TPAs deal commercially with the insurer and are not consumers of its services.

t: The Explanation to Section 2(7) relating to 'commercial purpose' applies to:
o: Goods bought and used exclusively for earning a livelihood by self-employment
e: The Explanation clarifies that for sub-clause (i) (goods), 'commercial purpose' does not include use by a consumer of goods bought and used exclusively for earning his livelihood by means of self-employment.

t: Which of the following defences is available to a product seller under the 2019 Act?
o: The seller is an e-commerce platform
The seller did not earn a profit
The product was misused, altered or modified by the consumer
e: The Act provides exceptions for sellers, including where the product has been misused, altered or modified; being a platform is not a defence.

t: A fairness-cream manufacturer convicted of a first misleading advertisement is fined ₹10 lakh. Two years later it repeats the offence. The maximum fine and imprisonment now are:
e: For a subsequent offence the fine may extend to ₹50 lakh and imprisonment to five years.

t: To avoid liability for a misleading advertisement, the 2019 Act expects an endorser to:
o: Obtain CCPA approval before the shoot
Exercise due diligence to verify the veracity of the claims made in the advertisement
e: The Act places an onus on endorsers to verify the claims they endorse; due diligence is the basis on which an endorser can refute liability.

t: Mediation under the 2019 Act is intended primarily to:
o: Provide quicker, simpler dispute settlement and reduce the pendency burden on consumer courts
e: Mediation was introduced as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism to make adjudication simpler and quicker and relieve the heavy pendency in consumer courts.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Section 147(1)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires that a policy complying with Chapter XI must be issued by:
o: An insurer approved by the State Transport Authority
Any insurer registered with the Registrar of Companies
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 147(1)(a) mandates that the policy be issued by a person who is an 'authorised insurer', a term defined in Section 145.

t: A group mediclaim policy with premium of ₹2.3 crore is the subject of a complaint by the policyholder company for deficiency in service. The complaint lies before the:
e: Consideration exceeding ₹2 crore places the complaint within the NCDRC's original jurisdiction under Section 58(1)(a)(i).

t: The upper limit of the State Commission's original jurisdiction over unfair contracts under Section 47(1)(a)(ii) is:
e: The State Commission hears unfair-contract complaints where consideration does not exceed ₹10 crore; above that the NCDRC has jurisdiction.

t: The Consumer Protection (Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulations, 2020 are relevant in the material chiefly because they:
o: Fix the pecuniary jurisdiction of Commissions
Prescribe time limits for review (30 days), revision (90 days) and second appeal (30 days)
e: Regulation 14(1) of the 2020 Regulations fixes 90 days for revision, 30 days for review and 30 days for second appeal, periods the Act itself does not specify.

t: Against an order of the NCDRC passed under Section 72 for non-compliance, an appeal lies to the Supreme Court under Section 73(1)(c) within:
e: Section 73 provides 30 days for appeals against non-compliance orders at every level, with power to condone delay.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: The bodily-injury cover in Section 147(1)(b)(i) extends to 'any person'. This expression has been read to include:
o: Persons outside the vehicle as well as the owner of goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle
e: The clause covers death or bodily injury to any person, and the 1994 amendment expressly added the owner of goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle.

t: A tempo-traveller (contract carriage) carrying passengers meets with an accident after the 2019 amendment. The passengers' injuries are:
o: Covered only under the Employees' Compensation Act
Not covered, as it is not a stage carriage
Covered under amended Section 147(1)(b)(ii) as passengers of a transport vehicle
e: The amended clause mandates cover for death or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle (other than gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle), which includes a contract carriage.

t: A ticket examiner of a bus is injured while checking tickets in the running bus. Under the proviso to Section 147(1) the Act policy covers him:
o: Only to the extent of liability under the Workmen's/Employees' Compensation Act
Only if he was a fare-paying passenger
As a third party without limit
e: Proviso (i)(b) covers persons engaged as conductor or in examining tickets on a public service vehicle only for Compensation Act liability.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Limits of liability
t: Under the old Section 147(2), the two limits of compulsory liability were:
o: The amount of liability incurred for death/injury, and ₹6,000 for third-party property damage
₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt
₹6,000 for death and unlimited for property
e: Clause (a) required cover for the amount of liability incurred (unlimited) for death or bodily injury, and clause (b) fixed ₹6,000 for damage to third-party property.

t: Under Section 64VA, the control level of solvency (required solvency ratio) that an insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64VA requires assets to exceed liabilities by the required solvency margin; IRDAI prescribes a control level solvency ratio of 150% (1.5 times), below which regulatory action follows.

t: Which sub-section of amended Section 147 preserves policies issued before the 2019 Amendment Act on their existing terms?
e: Amended sub-section (4) states that a policy issued before commencement of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 continues on existing terms as if the Act had not been amended.

t: A cover note expired on 15 September without a policy being issued. The branch informs the RTO on 25 September. Has Section 147 been complied with?
o: Yes, as no time limit is prescribed
No, as intimation should have gone to IRDAI
Yes, since intimation was within 30 days
No, as the intimation had to be made within 7 days of expiry, i.e. by 22 September
e: The insurer must notify the registering authority within seven days of expiry of the cover note's validity; 25 September is beyond the 22 September deadline.

t: A car reverses out of a private driveway onto a public road and injures a pedestrian on the footpath. The act causing the accident is the reversing from the driveway. Under the Explanation to Section 147, cover depends on whether:
o: The car was insured for own damage
The pedestrian was a third party
The act or omission that led to the accident occurred in a public place
e: The Explanation hinges on the location of the act or omission leading to the accident; where the negligent act occurs on or into a public road, the use is deemed to be in a public place.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Which of the following statements about the certificate of insurance under Section 147(3) is correct?
o: It is issued by the insurer in favour of the person by whom the policy is effected
It is optional for private cars
It is issued by the registering authority
e: The insurer issues the certificate in favour of the person effecting the policy; it supplements, not replaces, the policy and is required for the policy to have effect under Chapter XI.

t: The insurer's statutory obligation under Section 147(5)/(6) is to indemnify:
o: The person or classes of persons specified in the policy, for the liability the policy purports to cover
e: The sub-section obliges the insurer to indemnify the insured person or classes of persons specified in the policy for the liability the policy purports to cover, notwithstanding any other law.

t: The insured's employee is killed while travelling as a passenger in the insured's private car on office work. Under the proviso to Section 147(1), the compulsory policy:
o: Need not cover his death beyond Compensation Act liability, as he is an employee
Must cover him, because the employee-exclusion applies only to drivers, conductors/ticket examiners of PSVs and employees carried in goods carriages
e: The proviso's employee exclusion is confined to three categories; an employee travelling in a private car is not among them and is covered as any other person under Section 147(1)(b)(i).

t: Compensation under Section 164 (no fault) and a claim under Section 166 (fault-based) for the same death:
o: Must both be filed within 30 days
Can both be recovered in full
Are alternatives; amounts paid under Section 164 are adjusted against any award under Section 166
e: Section 164 provides interim no-fault compensation; where the claimant pursues a Section 166 claim, the amount paid under Section 164 is deducted from the final award.

t: The 'golden hour' under Section 2(12A) of the amended MV Act means:
o: The hour within which the police must reach the spot
The hour within which the insurer must appoint a surveyor
The one-hour period following a traumatic injury during which prompt medical care is most likely to prevent death
e: Section 2(12A) defines golden hour as the one-hour period following a traumatic injury; Section 162 requires schemes for cashless treatment of victims during this period.

t: Under Section 150 (earlier 149) of the MV Act, which of the following is a defence available to the insurer against a third-party award?
o: The insured did not pay the own-damage premium
The claim was filed after 3 months
The vehicle was driven by a person not duly licensed, or used for a purpose not permitted by the permit, in breach of a specified policy condition
e: The insurer may defend a third-party claim only on the statutory grounds, e.g. breach of specified conditions such as unlicensed driver, use for hire/reward not permitted, or policy obtained by non-disclosure.

t: A claimant accepts the insurer's settlement offer made under amended Section 149. The insurer must pay the agreed amount within:
e: Under amended Section 149, if the claimant accepts the offer within 30 days, the insurer makes payment within 30 days and the Tribunal records the settlement.

t: Which of these is NOT among the employee categories listed in the proviso to Section 147(1)?
o: Employee engaged in driving the vehicle
Conductor of a public service vehicle
Employee being carried in a goods carriage
Mechanic repairing the vehicle in the insured's garage
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The proviso names drivers, conductors/ticket examiners of a public service vehicle and employees carried in a goods carriage; a garage mechanic is not listed.

t: A repeat offender is caught driving an uninsured vehicle for the second time. Under Section 196 as amended, the fine is:
e: Section 196 provides a fine of ₹2,000 (or imprisonment up to 3 months) for a first offence and ₹4,000 for a second or subsequent offence.

t: A policyholder wants to assign his marine cargo policy to the bank financing the consignment. The assignment is governed by:
e: Section 38 governs assignment or transfer of policies by endorsement on the policy or by a separate instrument, with notice to the insurer.

t: Section 2(6B) of the Insurance Act, 1938 defines 'general insurance business' as:
o: Fire, marine or miscellaneous insurance business, whether carried on singly or in combination
e: Section 2(6B) defines general insurance business as fire, marine or miscellaneous insurance business, carried on singly or in combination.

t: A motor own-damage claim is estimated at ₹45,000. Under Section 64UM read with the regulations, the branch:
o: May settle without a licensed surveyor, since motor claims up to ₹50,000 do not require one
e: The surveyor threshold is ₹50,000 for motor and ₹1 lakh for other classes; a ₹45,000 motor claim may be assessed in-house.

t: Section 40 of the Insurance Act, 1938 (as amended) relates to:
o: Payment of commission or remuneration only to licensed/registered intermediaries, within limits specified by IRDAI
e: Section 40 prohibits payment of commission or remuneration except to duly registered agents/intermediaries and within the limits specified by IRDAI regulations.

t: An insurer's solvency ratio falls to 130%. Under Section 64VA and IRDAI norms the insurer:
o: Has breached the 150% control level and must submit a financial plan to IRDAI
e: The control level of solvency is 150%; an insurer below it must submit a financial plan to IRDAI, which may restrict its business.

t: The Insurance Advisory Committee constituted under the IRDA Act, 1999 may have a maximum of:
e: Section 25 of the IRDA Act provides for an Insurance Advisory Committee of not more than 25 members (excluding ex-officio members) to advise the Authority on regulations.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 framework, a general insurance policyholder who cancels a one-year policy mid-term (no claim) is entitled to:
o: Refund of proportionate premium for the unexpired period
e: The 2024 Master Circular allows the policyholder to cancel at any time by giving 7 days' notice, with refund of proportionate premium for the unexpired period where no claim has been made.

t: Under the 2024 regulations, an insurer should collect all documents required for claim processing:
o: At the time of claim intimation
At the underwriting stage, so that claims are not rejected for want of documents already available
e: The regulations require insurers to collect necessary documents at the proposal/underwriting stage and bar rejection of claims for want of documents that should have been collected then.

t: Under the 2021 amendment to the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, complaints can be made against:
o: Insurers, and also insurance intermediaries such as agents and brokers
e: The 2021 amendment brought intermediaries (agents, brokers and other insurance intermediaries) within the Ombudsman's jurisdiction and enabled online complaints and video hearings.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: A policyholder has a claim dispute of ₹48 lakh. He wants a fast, free resolution. He may approach the Insurance Ombudsman because:
o: Claims below ₹50 lakh can be brought and no fee is payable
The Ombudsman can award punitive damages
The Ombudsman sits in every district
e: The Ombudsman handles complaints up to ₹50 lakh free of cost; the award binds the insurer but the complainant remains free to approach other fora.

t: The maximum aggregate liability of the insurer under a Public Liability Insurance Act policy for more than one accident in a policy year is:
e: The PLI Rules provide ₹5 crore per accident and ₹15 crore in aggregate for all accidents during the policy year.

t: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 was enacted mainly in response to:
o: The Bhopal gas tragedy, to provide immediate relief to victims of hazardous-substance accidents
e: Post-Bhopal, the Act provides immediate no-fault relief to persons affected by accidents involving hazardous substances handled by an owner.

t: A 35-year-old employee (relevant factor 197.06) earning ₹18,000 per month suffers permanent total disablement. Compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act is:
e: Wages are capped at ₹15,000. PTD = 60% × 15,000 × 197.06 = ₹17,73,540, which exceeds the minimum of ₹1,40,000.

t: The statutory minimum compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act for death and permanent total disablement respectively is:
e: Section 4 fixes minimum compensation of ₹1,20,000 for death and ₹1,40,000 for permanent total disablement, payable if the formula amount is lower.

t: A claim for compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act must ordinarily be filed with the Commissioner within:
o: 2 years of the accident or death
e: Section 10 requires the claim within two years of the occurrence of the accident or death, with power to entertain late claims for sufficient cause.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: Under Section 19 of the Indian Contract Act, a contract induced by fraud or misrepresentation is:
o: Voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused
e: Section 19 makes such a contract voidable at the option of the deceived party, which is why an insurer may avoid a policy obtained by non-disclosure.

t: Under Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 an arbitral award, once the time for challenge has expired, is enforced:
o: Only after confirmation by the High Court
As if it were a decree of the court
e: Section 36 provides that the award is enforceable in the same manner as a decree of the court under the Code of Civil Procedure.

t: A proposer pays ₹75,000 of premium in cash for a shopkeeper's policy. Under IRDAI AML guidelines the branch must obtain:
o: PAN or Form 60 of the proposer, as cash premium exceeds ₹50,000
e: AML guidelines require PAN or Form 60 where cash premium exceeds ₹50,000 (and the aggregate cash is below the ₹2 lakh ceiling under Section 269ST of the Income-tax Act).

t: The agency to which insurers file Cash Transaction Reports and Suspicious Transaction Reports under the PMLA is:
e: FIU-IND, under the Ministry of Finance, receives CTRs (by the 15th of the succeeding month) and STRs from reporting entities, including insurers.

t: An RTI applicant seeks a competitor's underwriting data held by a PSU insurer. The PIO may refuse under Section 8(1)(d) because the information:
o: Involves commercial confidence or trade secrets whose disclosure would harm the competitive position of a third party
Was received from a foreign government
e: Section 8(1)(d) exempts commercial confidence, trade secrets or intellectual property whose disclosure would harm a third party's competitive position, unless larger public interest warrants disclosure.
